summary: The Gaussian first-order rate coefficient following (1.24) conflicts with the exact rate formulas; no core convergence conclusion shown false.

problems.location: physical/printed p7 paragraph following (1.24), using (1.19) p6 and (1.23) p7
problems.claim: For alphaU=betaU=a and alphaV=betaV=b, r has first-order term epsilon(a+b)/2.
problems.assumptions: a,b,epsilon>0; d>=1; isotropic centered Gaussian marginals N(0,a^-1 I), N(0,b^-1 I); nonnegative quadratic cost; all Theorem1.1 moments/smoothness and Corollary1.3 Hessian conditions hold; epsilon sqrt(kX kY)>2.
problems.decisive_evidence: Let q=sqrt(1+4/(epsilon^2 a b)); kX=a(q+1), kY=b(q+1). Then 1-4/(epsilon^2 kX kY)=2/(q+1), and r=2epsilon(a+b) exactly.
problems.counterexample: a=b=1 yields r=4epsilon rather than epsilon for every epsilon>0.
problems.counterevidence: Linear order remains correct; smaller rate is a valid conservative bound, but not the first-order coefficient of the defined r. No theorem damage demonstrated.
problems.core_dependency: No downstream proof dependency on the erroneous explanatory coefficient found in inspected Sections1.2.1 and5.1-5.2.
problems.impact: Local quantitative interpretation only; not a refutation of the convergence theorem.
problems.correction: Replace the coefficient by 2epsilon(alphaU+alphaV) under these Gaussian equalities; do not alter (1.19)/(1.23).

limitations: Claim-focused review; not exhaustive proof certification.

problems.source_claim: The paragraph after (1.24), PDF page 7, states the first-order coefficient epsilon(a+b)/2 for r defined in (1.19) and (1.23).
problems.hypotheses: Centered isotropic Gaussian marginals with Hessians a I and b I, a,b>0, epsilon>0, quadratic nonnegative cost, any d>=1; all stated moment, smoothness and curvature conditions hold. epsilon*sqrt(A*B)>2 follows from q>sqrt(q^2-1).
problems.independent_argument: Set q=sqrt(1+4/(epsilon^2*a*b)); (1.23) gives A=a(q+1), B=b(q+1). Then 4/(epsilon^2*A*B)=(q-1)/(q+1), hence r=epsilon*(A+B)*2/(q+1)=2*epsilon*(a+b), exactly. For a=b=1, r=4*epsilon, four times the printed first-order value.
problems.counterevidence: The stated linear order and conservative slower convergence bound remain valid. Source proofs on pages 39-40 use the displayed exact r and LSI constants, not the erroneous explanatory coefficient.
problems.impact_and_severity: A local quantitative specialization is false; the checked projected-LSI and corollary derivations do not depend on it. Minor rests on this dependency boundary, not repair difficulty.
problems.repair: The local exact replacement 2*epsilon*(a+b) is proved; no alteration of the core displayed rate is warranted.
